original_question: How can the invariant theory for long virtual knots be strengthened, including by combining Manturov's long-knot ideas with biquandle constructions, by extracting new classical knot invariants from long-knot methods, and by using the descending-diagram construction D(F) associated to a long flat virtual knot F to approach the broader problem of classifying long flat knots?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 7, "Long Knots and Long Flat Knots," i.e. the paper’s official problem about enlarging long-knot invariants, extracting new classical invariants from long-knot methods, and using the descending-diagram construction for long flat virtual knots toward classification. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual intent: it keeps the focus on long knots/long flat knots, mentions Manturov’s long-knot invariant structure, asks about obtaining new classical knot invariants from long-knot methods, invokes the descending diagram D(F) for a long flat virtual knot, and connects this with the full classification problem for long flat knots. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is the bundled Section 7, Problem 7, not just the general classification of flat virtual knots: the paper explicitly ties together three tasks—enlarging Manturov’s long-knot invariant structure, seeking new classical invariants, and exploiting Turaev’s descending construction for long flats. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

A long knot should be defined as a 1-1 tangle obtained by breaking a knot and taking its two ends to infinity along the horizontal axis; this is the framework in which the paper formulates the problem. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The classical-invariant clause needs the paper’s precise motivation: there is a natural map from long virtual knots to oriented compact virtual knots, and although this map has no inverse in general, it does have an inverse for classical knots, which is why long techniques may yield new classical invariants. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

A long flat virtual knot diagram F should be defined using Section 2.1: flat crossings are undecorated 4-valent nodes, virtual crossings are marked with a small circle, and equivalence is by generalized flat Reidemeister moves. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The construction D(F) needs its exact rule: one resolves each flat (non-virtual) crossing so that, in traversing the long diagram, one always goes over before going under. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The key invariant statement is missing from the draft: the long virtual knot type of D(F), not merely the particular diagram D(F), is an invariant of the long flat knot F. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper also states the quantifier explicitly: for any invariant I of virtual knots, the value I[D(F)] is an invariant of the long flat knot F; the paper then suggests doing sample calculations of such invariants. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier issues arise in this problem; the missing stand-alone content is topological and diagrammatic rather than algebraic. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: In the setting of long knots viewed as 1-1 tangles, can one enlarge Manturov’s long-knot invariant structure by combining it with the biquandle construction to obtain more powerful invariants of long knots, determine whether these long-knot methods yield genuinely new classical knot invariants via the classical compact-to-long correspondence, and, for a long flat virtual knot diagram F, exploit Turaev’s descending diagram D(F)—obtained by resolving every flat (non-virtual) crossing so that one always goes over before going under, with the long virtual knot type of D(F) depending only on F—so that every virtual-knot invariant I produces a long-flat invariant I[D(F)], with the aim of carrying out effective sample calculations toward the full classification of long flat knots? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft almost paraphrases the paper’s official Problem 7. The surrounding material needed to make that problem stand-alone comes from Section 2.1, which defines flat virtual diagrams and the overlying/forgetful relationship between virtual and flat diagrams, and Section 2.2, which explains long knots as 1-1 tangles, why long-knot invariants matter, why new classical invariants are being sought, and why long flat virtual knots are accessible through the descending construction. That is the narrowest paper-faithful target matching your draft. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
